items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, talking right about this same period, Tim, I know you told me one time that you...

ctx.x: Your parents were Mexicans or Spanish? No, my parents were Mexicans and Spanish.

Well, talking right about this same period, Tim, I know you told me one time that you, I don't know how much you made, but you started on the tuba, I think, when you were about twelve, and a year later you actually made a little money playing on the darn thing.

On the tuba? No, no. Yeah. Bass fiddle? No, that was on the guitar. On the guitar? On the guitar. Well, I'll tell you about that. You see, there was a, you know, always a system here with the high color, with the Mexicans and the Puerto Ricans. That's what you haven't got to there. Well, that vanished a long time ago. It's serenading. Mm-hmm. Say sometime about, say, 10 o'clock, maybe until 10, 12, 1 o'clock in the morning. Well, if they were going to serenade a mother or they were going to serenade a sweetheart…
